import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Convert is_fraud to categorical for better visualization
df['is_fraud'] = pd.Categorical(df['is_fraud']).codes

# Create a bar chart to compare the frequency of fraud and non-fraud transactions
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.countplot(x='is_fraud', data=df)
plt.title('Frequency of Fraud and Non-Fraud Transactions')
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Transaction Type')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to display the distribution of transaction amounts
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.histplot(df['amount'], kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Transaction Amounts')
plt.xlabel('Amount ($)')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.savefig('output_amount.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between hour_of_day and amount
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.scatterplot(x='hour_of_day', y='amount', data=df)
plt.title('Relationship between Hour of Day and Transaction Amount')
plt.xlabel('Hour of Day')
plt.ylabel('Amount ($)')
plt.savefig('output_hour_amount.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a pie chart to display the distribution of transaction types
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
df['transaction_type'].value_counts().plot(kind='pie', autopct='%1.1f%%')
plt.title('Distribution of Transaction Types')
plt.axis('equal')  # Equal aspect ratio ensures that pie is drawn as a circle.
plt.savefig('output_types.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
